models_evaluated: CT-based deep learning algorithm for extranodal extension prediction

links.outcome: Deep learning algorithm AUC for ENE versus four head and neck radiologists on same data
links.effect: Algorithm AUC 0·86 (95% CI 0·82-0·90), outperforming all readers (p<0·0001 for each); radiologist kappa 0·32.
links.quote: The deep learning algorithm AUC for ENE classification was 0·86 (95% CI 0·82-0·90), outperforming all readers (p<0·0001 for each).

links.outcome: Algorithm sensitivity at different false positive rate operating points compared with best reader
links.effect: Matching specificity to best reader (FPR 22%) gave 75% sensitivity (+13%); FPR 30% gave 90% sensitivity.
links.quote: Setting the algorithm false positive rate to 30% yielded 90% sensitivity.

screen.reason: Retrospective reader study evaluating a deep learning algorithm's diagnostic performance for predicting extranodal extension on CT scans compared to four radiologists; it does not evaluate a specific organizational deployment practice or safeguard.
